transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I’m here because something at work has been going on for months, and I know it sounds technical, but I’m an interpreter and I work with translation files, memories, timestamps, all that. I keep seeing the same pattern in the project files—tiny changes, not obvious ones. Certain subcontractors, and one colleague in particular, keep adjusting the translation memory and the timestamps so it looks like my quality control failed.

And IT keeps saying the audit trail is clean, but… that’s exactly the point. If the record is arranged properly, it would look clean. It’s like when you label folders a certain way and no one notices one is out of sequence—I used to do that in grad school with reference files, actually. Anyway, the result is that the blame lands on me, and I can’t just ignore that anymore.
Are you certain that your colleague is deliberately altering the files to make you look responsible?

Yes, I’m certain. I mean… not in the sense that I caught him with his hands on the keyboard, but the pattern is too consistent. For months I’ve been seeing these tiny changes in the translation memory and the timestamps, and it always ends up making it look like my quality control failed.

It’s like—sorry, this is a bit like when you compare two versions of a glossary and one term has shifted just enough to cause problems later. Most people wouldn’t notice unless they knew what to look for. And IT keeps saying the audit trail is clean, but that doesn’t reassure me. To me, that just means the record has been arranged well enough that the blame lands on me.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is there?

I don’t think so… I mean, not voices like someone standing in the room talking when no one’s there. Sometimes I’ll replay conversations in my head, especially from work, because I’m trying to remember exact wording—interpreters do that a lot, or at least I do. It’s like checking a transcript mentally.

But hearing a voice out loud? No, I haven’t noticed anything like that.
Have you recently had a period where you felt unusually energized and needed much less sleep than usual?

I’m not sure I’d call it unusually energized. I’ve had nights where I sleep badly because I’m going over work details in my head, but that’s different, I think. Like when you’re trying to remember whether a term was approved in one glossary or another, and then suddenly it’s 2 a.m. and you’re still thinking about file versions.

But needing much less sleep and feeling great or charged up because of it… I don’t think I’ve noticed that, no.
Do you believe your colleague can change the files in a way that is impossible with normal computer access?

Impossible with normal access… I don’t know if I’d put it that way. I’m not saying he has some magical access or anything like that. It’s more that the changes are so small and placed so carefully—translation memory entries, timestamps, the kind of things most people would skip over—that by the time anyone looks, it all seems clean.

That’s what bothers me. IT says the audit trail is fine, but I’ve worked with these project files for years. You start recognizing patterns, like when a subcontractor keeps using the same wrong term and then suddenly the blame traces back to my review. Sorry, that’s maybe not exactly your question. I just mean… I think the record has been arranged in a way that makes me look responsible, whether or not IT calls it “normal access.”
If clear proof showed that no one had altered the files, would you accept that?

I mean… if it was clear proof, real proof, I’d have to look at it. I’m not trying to ignore evidence. But that’s the thing—people keep saying “the audit trail is clean,” and that doesn’t answer what I’m seeing.

For months it’s been the same pattern in the project files. Tiny changes in the translation memory, timestamps that line up too neatly, certain subcontractors’ errors somehow ending up looking like my quality control missed them. And one colleague is always near it, somehow. It’s not like a dramatic thing, it’s small, procedural—like how a comma in the wrong place changes the meaning, you know?

So if someone showed me proof no one altered anything… I’d want to know what they were calling “altered.” Because the record can still be arranged to put the blame on me even if IT says nothing was changed.
Apart from this problem at work, do you believe anyone else is trying to harm, monitor, or conspire against you?

No, not really outside of work. I mean, I don’t think strangers are following me or anything like that.

It’s this work situation. For months I keep seeing the same pattern in the project files—certain subcontractors making these little errors, and then one colleague being connected to these tiny changes in the translation memory or timestamps, so later it looks like my quality control failed. And then when I try to explain it, people say, “Well, IT checked the audit trail,” as if that settles it.

Sorry, I know you asked about anyone else. I guess my answer is no, not apart from that. It’s not some broad conspiracy. It’s the files, the record being arranged so the blame lands on me.
Have you become less interested in seeing other people or doing your usual activities?

Not generally, no. I mean, I still do my work, I still translate, keep the team workflow moving, pay bills, do the usual family things.

Sometimes I get pulled into it when the file history comes up, or when certain coworkers’ names are attached to a project, and then I can lose a lot of time trying to understand what happened. But outside of that specific project issue, I’m not sitting at home avoiding everyone or giving up my normal routines.
Before this started at work, did you generally find it hard to trust other people?

I don’t know… generally? I mean, I’ve always been careful with people, I guess, but I wouldn’t say I walked around thinking everyone was untrustworthy.

It depends what you mean by trust, though. Like, in translation work, you learn to check everything—source text, terminology, context—because one small assumption can throw the whole thing off. My father used to say something similar about measuring twice before cutting wood, which is funny because he was not precise at all with paperwork.

But before this work issue, no, I don’t think I had some big problem trusting people. Not that I noticed, anyway.
For about how long have you been convinced that your colleague is arranging the files to make you look responsible?

About… eleven months, I think. It was shortly after they put me in charge of that new localization project.

At first I thought it was just normal project mess, because new workflows always have little snags—terminology tables, handoffs, all that—but then the same kinds of file changes kept turning up. So, yes, roughly 11 months.
Before this started at work, did you often suspect that other people were trying to take advantage of you or harm you?

Before this? I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I mean, everybody has moments where you wonder if someone is being fair, or if they’re trying to get the better end of a deal—buying a car, dealing with a landlord, that kind of thing.

But often? Harm me? No, I don’t think that was how I moved through life. I was cautious, maybe. My mother always called it “checking the seams,” like with clothes before you buy them, which is odd because she’d buy things with missing buttons and then complain later.

So… no, not really. Not in some constant way before the work situation.
Has anyone shown you specific evidence that your colleague did not alter the files?

IT said the audit trail was clean, yes. They showed me that, or at least they summarized it. But that isn’t the same as proof nothing happened.

I mean, with translation memory systems, if you know the workflow, you can make a tiny change at the right point and then everything later looks normal. It’s like when you revise a sentence and the final version doesn’t show how it got bent out of shape. Sorry, that’s probably too much detail.

So yes, they’ve said there’s no evidence my colleague altered the files. But I don’t think that clears it, because the pattern is still there—the timestamps, the little changes, the subcontractors’ files lining up in a way that makes it look like my quality control failed. That doesn’t happen by accident for months.
Have you felt that someone can put thoughts into your mind?

Put thoughts into my mind? I don’t think so… I mean, people can influence you. Like if someone keeps saying a phrase in a meeting, then later you find yourself using it, which happens a lot in translation work because wording sticks to you.

But if you mean literally, like thoughts being placed there that aren’t mine… no, I haven’t really noticed anything like that. My thoughts feel like my own, even when I’m going over things too much.
Has there been any moment when you were completely certain your colleague was not altering the files?

Completely certain? No… I don’t think there’s been a moment like that. I can have moments where I think, all right, maybe I’m tired, maybe I’m seeing too much in the files—but then I look again and it’s the same pattern.

It’s not just one typo or one timestamp. It’s months of certain subcontractors’ files lining up with my colleague’s changes, tiny things in the translation memory, the timing of it, and then somehow it all points back at my quality control. IT says the audit trail is clean, but that doesn’t settle it for me. Records can be arranged to look clean. I’ve seen enough of the project files to know something was being set up to put the blame on me.

Sorry, I’m circling. But no, I’ve never been completely certain he wasn’t altering them.
Have other people told you that your speech or thinking has become hard to follow or seems disorganized?

I’m not sure. No one’s really said, “You’re disorganized,” not in those words.

Sometimes people ask me to slow down or get to the point, especially at work, but that happens in translation meetings too because everyone is jumping between source text, target text, deadlines, who changed what… it’s not exactly normal conversation. My sister once said I explain things like I’m footnoting myself, which I suppose I do.

But hard to follow? Maybe when I’m trying to explain the file issue, because there are a lot of pieces. I don’t think people mean my thinking is disorganized, more that they don’t have the background to follow the chain.
Do you believe it is possible that you might be mistaken about your colleague altering the files?

I suppose anything is “possible,” in the way that, you know, a translator can misread a sentence if the context is wrong. I’ve had that happen—one word changes the whole meaning, and then you go back and think, how did I not see that?

But with this… I don’t think I’m mistaken. I’m here because for months I’ve been seeing the same pattern in the project files. It’s not one odd mistake. It’s certain subcontractors, and one colleague, making these tiny changes in the translation memory and the timestamps, and then somehow it ends up looking like my quality control failed.

IT keeps saying the audit trail is clean, but that doesn’t reassure me. A clean-looking record can be arranged that way. That’s kind of the point. So… yes, in some abstract sense I could be wrong, but I don’t believe I am.
Have you ever seen things that other people could not see?

Seen things other people couldn’t see? I don’t think so… not like seeing a person in the room who isn’t there, if that’s what you mean.

I mean, sometimes I notice things other people miss, especially in text or formatting. A misplaced punctuation mark, a strange timestamp, a segment that doesn’t match the source properly—translators get trained to see that. My wife says I can spot a typo from across the room but forget where I put my keys, which is probably fair.

But actual things that no one else can see… no, I haven’t noticed anything like that.
Have you had a strong sense that there is a special message meant specifically for you in things like TV, radio, newspapers, or online posts?

Not TV or radio, no… I don’t sit there thinking the news anchor is talking to me or anything like that.

Online posts can be tricky, though, because work is online now—shared files, comments, version histories, all of that. It’s not a “message” exactly, it’s more the pattern. For months I’ve been seeing it in the project files: certain subcontractors and one colleague making these tiny changes to the translation memory, the timestamps, the kind of things most people wouldn’t notice. Then somehow it makes it look like my quality control failed.

And when IT says the audit trail is clean… well, that doesn’t really answer it, because a clean record can be arranged. That’s what makes it hard to explain. It’s not like a newspaper headline saying my name, it’s more like the files are being set up so the blame points at me.

It’s months of certain subcontractors’ files lining up with my colleague’s changes, tiny things in the translation memory, the timing of it, and then somehow it all points back at my quality control. IT says the audit trail is clean, but that doesn’t settle it for me. Records can be arranged to look clean. I’ve seen enough of the project files to know something was being set up to put the blame on me.

Sorry, I’m circling. But no, I’ve never been completely certain he wasn’t altering them.

doctor.intent: Assess whether there are disorganized or negative symptoms suggestive of schizophrenia rather than delusional disorder or paranoid personality disorder.
doctor.question: Have other people told you that your speech or thinking has become hard to follow or seems disorganized?

target_item.reason: The question is about whether others have noticed disorganized speech or thinking, but the provided symptom profile covers delusions, functioning, impairment, and duration—not disorganized speech or thought process.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure. No one’s really said, “You’re disorganized,” not in those words.

Sometimes people ask me to slow down or get to the point, especially at work, but that happens in translation meetings too because everyone is jumping between source text, target text, deadlines, who changed what… it’s not exactly normal conversation. My sister once said I explain things like I’m footnoting myself, which I suppose I do.

But hard to follow? Maybe when I’m trying to explain the file issue, because there are a lot of pieces. I don’t think people mean my thinking is disorganized, more that they don’t have the background to follow the chain.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the fixed persecutory belief is held with delusional conviction despite contrary evidence, which best distinguishes delusional disorder from paranoid personality disorder and schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Do you believe it is possible that you might be mistaken about your colleague altering the files?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for months I’ve been seeing the same pattern in the project files—certain subcontractors and one colleague keep making tiny changes to the translation memory and timestamps so it looks like my quality control failed, and even when IT says the audit trail is clean, I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about whether the belief about the colleague altering files can be doubted or revised, which directly assesses the fixed nature of the delusion.

patient.answer:
I suppose anything is “possible,” in the way that, you know, a translator can misread a sentence if the context is wrong. I’ve had that happen—one word changes the whole meaning, and then you go back and think, how did I not see that?

But with this… I don’t think I’m mistaken. I’m here because for months I’ve been seeing the same pattern in the project files. It’s not one odd mistake. It’s certain subcontractors, and one colleague, making these tiny changes in the translation memory and the timestamps, and then somehow it ends up looking like my quality control failed.

IT keeps saying the audit trail is clean, but that doesn’t reassure me. A clean-looking record can be arranged that way. That’s kind of the point. So… yes, in some abstract sense I could be wrong, but I don’t believe I am.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the fixed persecutory belief is occurring without prominent hallucinations or formal thought disorder, which would favor delusional disorder over schizophrenia or schizotypal/paranoid personality pathology.
doctor.question: Have you ever seen things that other people could not see?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about visual hallucinations (seeing things others cannot see), but the provided symptom profile only covers delusions, functioning, impairment, and duration.

patient.answer:
Seen things other people couldn’t see? I don’t think so… not like seeing a person in the room who isn’t there, if that’s what you mean.

I mean, sometimes I notice things other people miss, especially in text or formatting. A misplaced punctuation mark, a strange timestamp, a segment that doesn’t match the source properly—translators get trained to see that. My wife says I can spot a typo from across the room but forget where I put my keys, which is probably fair.

But actual things that no one else can see… no, I haven’t noticed anything like that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the persecutory belief is non-bizarre and encapsulated rather than part of a broader schizophrenic psychosis, helping distinguish delusional disorder from paranoid schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Have you had a strong sense that there is a special message meant specifically for you in things like TV, radio, newspapers, or online posts?

patient.answer:
Not TV or radio, no… I don’t sit there thinking the news anchor is talking to me or anything like that.

Online posts can be tricky, though, because work is online now—shared files, comments, version histories, all of that. It’s not a “message” exactly, it’s more the pattern. For months I’ve been seeing it in the project files: certain subcontractors and one colleague making these tiny changes to the translation memory, the timestamps, the kind of things most people wouldn’t notice. Then somehow it makes it look like my quality control failed.

And when IT says the audit trail is clean… well, that doesn’t really answer it, because a clean record can be arranged. That’s what makes it hard to explain. It’s not like a newspaper headline saying my name, it’s more like the files are being set up so the blame points at me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a fixed, non-bizarre persecutory belief focused on a coworker allegedly manipulating work files to make the patient appear at fault, persisting for about 11 months despite contrary IT findings. There is no evidence of hallucinations, thought insertion, prominent disorganization, negative symptoms, broad paranoid pattern predating the episode, or functional decline outside the delusional theme. This most strongly supports persistent delusional disorder rather than paranoid personality disorder or schizophrenia.
